chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is disliked for the fasting person to immerse himself in water.

key_terms.فِي الْمَاءِ: In the water - referring to fresh water typically used for purification.
key_terms.لِلصَّائِمِ: For the fasting person - referring to one observing sawm.
key_terms.يَرْتَمِسَ: To immerse oneself - specifically dipping the whole body into water, often up to the neck.
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (makruh) - a juristic category indicating a recommended act of omission, where doing it is not sinful but omitting it is better.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a fasting person immersing themselves in water?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on expiation for Ramadan fasting, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the precautionary principle (ihtiyat) in fiqh, where full immersion (irtimas) is disliked to prevent accidental ingestion of water that could invalidate the fast. This ruling reflects the scholarly emphasis on preserving the integrity of the fast during acts of purification, distinguishing between mere washing and complete submersion.
